bottleneck.description: General-purpose collaborative robots (3-20kg payload) and best-selling MG400 desktop robot - a contested space with multiple Chinese (AUBO, JAKA) and global (UR, FANUC, ABB) substitutes.

dependency.key_customers: Distributors and end users in 80+ countries; ~60% of revenue exported (unusually export-heavy for a Chinese cobot maker); education, light manufacturing, electronics assembly customers
dependency.key_suppliers: Largely vertically integrated - Dobot designs its own controllers, servo drives, and encoders; upstream rare-earth permanent magnets, harmonic reducers, MCUs and power electronics are multi-sourced

editorial.notes: Despite Dobot's #2 global cobot share (~13%) behind Universal Robots, the cobot market is structurally fragmented. Three of the top four positions are Chinese (Dobot, AUBO, JAKA) with overlapping product lines, plus global incumbents (UR, FANUC, ABB, KUKA, Yaskawa, Techman, Doosan, Franka). Switching between cobot vendors is low-friction relative to industrial robots given simpler programming and shorter qualification cycles. Dobot's vertical integration of controllers/servos/encoders is a cost advantage, not a bottleneck for customers - substitutes are abundant. Maps directly to LOW calibration anchors (ABBN/6954 JP/SYM) as peer-competitive automation vendor.
